key_insight: The retrieval strategy (simple grep/keyword search vs. dense/RAG) strongly interacts with agent architecture and tool-calling; a context-adaptive “Reshape” retrieval policy that routes between strategies yields the best trade-off of accuracy, latency, and cost.
problem_solved: Provides the first systematic comparison of retrieval strategies within agentic search systems and shows how retrieval choice plus tool-calling paradigm affects real-world agent performance and resource use.
method: Controlled experiments comparing multiple retrieval strategies (grep/keyword matching, dense retrieval, and RAG) across agent architectures and tool-calling setups.
Introduce Reshape: an adaptive retrieval policy that selects or composes retrieval modes based on task context, confidence, and downstream tool requirements.
Evaluate across benchmarks with metrics for task success, latency, token/cost, and robustness to noisy or large corpora.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners practical guidance to choose or combine retrieval methods for agent design, enabling more accurate, efficient, and cost-effective agentic systems.
visual_elements: Agent loop diagram showing retrieval → reasoning → tool call with branching for grep vs RAG (illustrates interaction)
Bar/line chart comparing accuracy, latency, and cost for grep, dense, RAG, and Reshape across tasks
Decision flowchart for Reshape policy (when to use grep, when to escalate to RAG or tool-call)
Heatmap or matrix showing performance sensitivity to agent architecture × retrieval strategy
paper_title: Is Grep All You Need? How Agent Harnesses Reshape Agentic Search
paper_authors: Sahil Sen, Akhil Kasturi, Elias Lumer, Anmol Gulati, Vamse Kumar Subbiah
